**Bartolomeus Jozef Lodewijk Rosalia** "**Bart** " **Somers** (born 12 May 1964 in [Mechelen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechelen "Mechelen"))[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-1) is a [Belgian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"), [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders") [politician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politician "Politician"). He is currently the [mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor "Mayor") of [Mechelen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechelen "Mechelen").
In 2017, Bart Somers was awarded 2016 [World Mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Mayor "World Mayor") Prize as recognition for his outstanding achievements in welcoming refugees during recent years and for the long-term integration of immigrants from different cultures, religions and social backgrounds.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-4) He obtained a law degree from the [Katholieke Universiteit Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katholieke_Universiteit_Leuven "Katholieke Universiteit Leuven").
## Political career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bart_Somers&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Political career")]
Bart Somers is the son of the former [People's Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Union_\(Belgium\) "People's Union \(Belgium\)") parliamentarian, Joos Somers,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-5) who was notably a deputy and a senator. After a law degree at KU Leuven, Bart Somers went through the Volksunie before joining the Open VLD in 1992.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-6)
Between 2003 and 2004, he was the [Minister-President of Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister-President_of_Flanders "Minister-President of Flanders").
After the [regional elections of June 2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Belgian_regional_elections "2004 Belgian regional elections") he was appointed the interim chairman of the [Flemish Liberals and Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Liberals_and_Democrats "Flemish Liberals and Democrats") (VLD). On 4 December 2004, he was elected with just over 50 percent of the vote to a full term as chairman.
Bart Somers was one of the three negotiators for the Open VLD during the [2007 Belgian government formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Belgian_government_formation "2007 Belgian government formation").
After his party's defeat in the [regional elections of 2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Belgian_regional_elections "2009 Belgian regional elections"), he resigned as chairman of the [Flemish Liberals and Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Liberals_and_Democrats "Flemish Liberals and Democrats").
In June 2016, the [European Committee of the Regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Committee_of_the_Regions "European Committee of the Regions") adopted Bart Somers report on "_Combatting Radicalisation and Violent Extremism: Prevention mechanisms at local and regional level_ ".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-7) His opinion won cross-party support for its calls for more effective policing, for more cooperation between local, regional, national and European authorities, and for an approach based on respect for core principles.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-9)
In October 2016, Bart Somers was elected as Leader of [the Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe in the European Committee of the Regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Alliance_of_Liberals_and_Democrats_for_Europe_in_the_European_Committee_of_the_Regions "The Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe in the European Committee of the Regions").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-10)
In February 2017, he received the "World Mayor Prize 2016", an election for the year's best mayor in the world.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-11)
In October 2019, he became Vice minister-president of the Flemish Government and Flemish Minister for Living Together and Domestic Administration in the [Jambon Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jambon_Government "Jambon Government").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-12) On November 6, 2023, he decided to resume his position and focus on his mayoralty of Mechelen.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bart_Somers#cite_note-13)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bart_Somers&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]
He was formerly married to Miet Bourlon (currently divorced) and he has two children, a girl Lieze and a boy Jan Klaas.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
